newsitem.title: GERMANY: German govt sees no need to dramatise forex moves.
newsitem.headline: German govt sees no need to dramatise forex moves.

text.p: The German government sees no reason to dramatise the recent developments in foreign exchange markets, government spokesman Peter Hausmann said at a news conference.

Hausmann told journalists at a regular government press briefing after a cabinet meeting on Wednesday that Germany remained in close contact with its G7 partners about the foreign exchange developments.

"From Germany's point of view there is no reason to dramatise developments," Hausmann said, adding that the mark's current weakness against the dollar and the pound should be seen as a result of the strong economies in the U.S. and Britain.
He said the Group of Seven industrial nations said in February in Berlin that the appreciation of the mark had been fully corrected.
"Together with our G7 partners we are closely observing developments on foreign exchange markets," Hausmann said.

Hausmann said the government believes exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals. He said the increase in the value of the dollar and pound reflected the economic conditions in the United States and Britain.
He said that Chancellor Helmut Kohl stressed at the cabinet meeting that the euro should be introduced on time in 1999 and that it would be a strong currency.
"Kohl stressed again in cabinet that the euro will come on time and the euro will be strong," Hausmann said.
He said the government believes speculation ahead of the planned launch of economic and monetary union (EMU) was affecting the foreign exchange markets.
